# Independent page-border recovery controls

Generated by `tools/page_border_recovery_fixture.py` from the project's original
`page-setting-recovery/healthy.docx` package. No private template, third-party
artwork or implementation source is redistributed. ZIP timestamps are fixed.

The two-section document includes styled paragraphs, numbering, a table, a
header and two original PNGs. Four differently colored single-line page borders
are added to each section. Each named variant changes one side to valid OOXML
`wave`, which the renderer currently does not implement. `combined` changes top
and right together. The corresponding `-omitted` control removes exactly those
sides; all other package content remains the same.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.6.10 defines each `pgBorders` child independently and keeps
common placement/display settings on the container. This change is explicitly
a read-only approximation, not support for wave or art borders and not a reference
divergence. Existing `page-borders` native controls remain the reference for
supported line placement, display and ordering.

Checks require strict rejection, localized diagnostics, retained section
geometry, rich content and supported border sides, exact pixel/line equality
with the omission controls, and download of the original bytes. Invalid values,
shadow declarations and nested side content are covered separately by unit
mutations. Duplicate sides, invalid container positioning or container text
remain whole-border failures because choosing their semantics would be ambiguous.
Unsafe editing/export remains unavailable. Corner geometry adjacent to an omitted
side follows the no-border approximation; no authored extent is invented.
